This comparison analyzes the type and volume of treatments with [[bmsl|Biologiske og målrettede syntetiske lægemidler]] (BMSL) across different age groups, serving as a key metric for [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]] [^src1]. The data provides a cross-sectional snapshot of treatment distribution between children (Børn) and adults (Voksne), highlighting which therapies dominate clinical practice and which remain on the margins.

Infliximab is the overwhelmingly dominant treatment across both demographics [^src1]. It accounts for 1,936 treatments in children (65% of the pediatric total) and 26,287 treatments in adults (43% of the adult total) [^src1]. Following infliximab, adalimumab is the second most common treatment for children with 470 cases (16%), while vedolizumab is the second most common for adults with 10,922 cases (18%) [^src1]. 

At the lower end of the spectrum, treatments like upadacitinib (6 pediatric cases) and ozanimod (7 pediatric cases) represent a tiny fraction of care, rounding to 0% in the pediatric cohort [^src1]. Notably, three treatments—filgotinib, mirikizumab, and ozanimod—record pediatric usage (67, 180, and 7 cases, respectively) but show completely blank entries for adult treatments [^src1]. This indicates either an absolute absence of adult prescriptions or unrecorded data for these specific drugs in the adult population, making them distinct outliers in the dataset [^src1]. 

In total, the dataset records 2,971 BMSL treatments for children and 61,190 for adults [^src1]. Because this comparison is drawn from a single dated section, no longitudinal trends regarding the rise or fall of specific drug preferences over time can be established.
